analysis.title: NVIDIA Corp: A Symbolic Show of Strength; We Have Cut '28, But Keep The Faith
key_insights: FQ3 revenue was $115.8B, 5-6% above both UBSe and the Street and well above NVDA's usual ~$2B/Q beat. Data Center was ~5% ahead of UBSe, led by hyperscale and ACIE (enterprise, neocloud). Edge Compute was ~14% ahead of UBSe.
FQ3 gross margin was 74.9%, near the top of the guidance range, and opex was ~$350MM below guidance. Non-GAAP EPS was $2.68 vs UBSe $2.53 and Street $2.48.

FQ4 revenue guidance is ~$130B at the midpoint with gross margin of 71-72%, in line with UBS's preview. F2028/C2027 revenue guidance was walked up slightly from 70% to 75%, also in line with the preview. Management said FQ4 is the gross margin bottom, with 72-73% for the full year.

FQ4 opex guidance of ~$10.7B was heavier than expected. UBS attributes ~$300MM to a shift from FQ3 and the extra week of a 14-week quarter, and estimates underlying FQ4 opex at ~$10.1B. Management indicated opex will keep growing in the high $100MMs Q/Q, putting FQ1 opex at $10.9-11.0B in UBS's view.

Total supply (balance sheet inventory plus supply and capacity commitments) rose from ~$311B in FQ2 to ~$430B. More than $100B of the increase was for F2028/C2027, backing the guidance raise and leaving C2027 seemingly fully covered for COGS.

Supply for F2029/C2028 and F2030/C2029 rose only slightly, unlike last quarter's large step-up in longer-term commitments. UBS says a big C2028 increase would have eased investor fears of a major growth deceleration.

UBS flags a risk that NVDA becomes beholden to purchase commitments and has to keep funding customers to drive revenue. It also flags talent retention after recent management changes as a legitimate concern.
Management's language on support for neoclouds sounded more measured ('disciplined and selective'), though the company says it remains committed.

NVDA will file its 10-Q 'in the coming weeks' instead of at the earnings release, as it had since F1Q25. Management tied the delay to the ongoing investigation and whether additional risk factors are needed. A supplemental financial information release replaced it for now.
Three direct customers were each over 10% of revenue (14%, 11%, 11%), vs one at 16% last quarter. Two U.S. frontier labs will be 15% of Data Center revenue this year combined, implying roughly $60B.
NVDA bought back ~$22B of stock vs UBS's $19B estimate and plans to execute the full $227B authorization by F2028, implying a run-rate of ~$45-50B per quarter.

FQ4 purchase commitments of $69B against implied COGS of ~$38B point to a possible large inventory build ahead of Rubin racks, unless the commitments land in later periods. Commitments were flat from Jan'26 to Jul'26 while COGS was ~$50B, which suggests timing mismatches that UBS will follow up on.

UBS makes minor tweaks to C2027, cuts C2028 EPS to $18.80 (from $20.01, revenue growth now under 10% Y/Y) and assumes C2029 is flat. The price target falls to $220 from $240 at an unchanged 12x C2028E P/E, the median of AI-exposed semis peers. Rating stays Buy.

market_movers.rationale: PT cut from $240 to $220 on lower C2028E EPS of $18.80 (from $20.01) at an unchanged 12x P/E. C2027 confidence is high after the supply commitment increase, but C2028 growth is under 10% Y/Y.

sector_views.rationale: The extra C2027 purchase commitments relieve the supply chain, but little was added for C2028, so questions about a slowdown are likely to persist.

earnings_insights: NVDA reported FQ3 revenue of $115.8B (reported), 5-6% above UBSe and Street consensus.
FQ3 non-GAAP EPS was $2.68 reported vs UBSe $2.53 and Street consensus $2.48.
FQ3 gross margin was 74.9% (reported), near the top of the guidance range. Opex was ~$350MM below guidance.
FQ3 networking/compute split was ~$21.3B (UBS estimate) / ~$86.3B, vs UBSe $18.3B / $84.7B.

FQ4 guidance (company): revenue ~$130B at the midpoint for a 14-week quarter, gross margin 71-72%, opex ~$10.7B. UBS estimates underlying opex at ~$10.1B after adjusting for the delayed ~$300MM and the extra week.
UBS estimates for FQ4 non-GAAP EPS are $2.94 (from $2.90) vs Street consensus $2.75. UBS FY01/27E EPS is $9.71 (from $9.52) vs consensus $9.29.
UBS FY01/28E EPS is $17.82 (from $17.11) vs consensus $15.73. UBS FY01/29E EPS is $18.80 (from $20.01) vs consensus $20.90.
NVDA bought back ~$22B of stock in FQ3 (reported) vs UBS's $19B estimate. It plans to execute the $227B authorization by F2028.
risk_factors: C2028 growth deceleration: supply commitments for F2029/C2028 barely increased.
NVDA may become beholden to purchase commitments and have to keep funding customers to drive revenue.
Talent retention after recent management changes.
Support for neoclouds sounded more measured ('disciplined and selective').
The delayed 10-Q is tied to the ongoing investigation and possible new risk factors.
A large FQ4 inventory build if the $69B of purchase commitments reach COGS or inventory in that quarter.
UBS's stated company risks: AMD competition in GPUs, ARM-based processor competition, and Intel competition in GPU computing.
vol_and_positioning: The stock closed at $155.46 on 17-Nov-2026, the bottom of its 52-week range ($239.24-$155.46). UBS cites investor worries about a big miss or rescinded C2027 guidance, and widespread fears of a major growth deceleration in C2028.
geopolitical: Recent licensing requirements in SE Asia: management said the impact is limited because customers are not changing plans, and NVDA will fill any offtake voids with other non-China customers.

tension_points.bull_case: Guidance raise and >$100B added to C2027 supply commitments show very high confidence in C2027, with the year seemingly fully covered for COGS. Buybacks are stepping up to ~$45-50B/Q.
tension_points.bear_case: C2028 supply commitments barely rose, so investor fears of a major growth deceleration persist. UBS now has C2028 revenue growth under 10% Y/Y and C2029 flat.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A large increase in F2029/C2028 supply commitments would ease the deceleration fears. Conversely, C2027 cuts would undermine the bull case.

theme_stances.key_argument: C2027 confidence is very high, but C2028 growth slows to under 10% Y/Y, so UBS cuts the PT only slightly and keeps Buy.
theme_stances.evidence: our view has always been that this is more about how much things decelerate in C2028
